title: HTTP Method Manipulation on get_favorite_restaurants Endpoint
description:
The /api/get_favorite_restaurants.php endpoint accepts all HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD) without proper validation. This endpoint is meant for retrieving data and should only accept GET requests, or at minimum reject non-standard methods with HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed) responses.

The endpoint processes all HTTP methods identically, returning "User not authenticated." responses regardless of which method was used. This indicates that method validation is not implemented and all requests are processed through the same code path regardless of the HTTP verb used.

Lack of HTTP method validation allows several attack vectors:
- HTTP method-based WAF bypass techniques that exploit method confusion
- HTTP request smuggling attacks that abuse method mishandling
- Potential logic flaws if the application contains conditional code based on methods
- CSRF attacks enabled by GET method acceptance on state-affecting operations
impact:
Attackers could use non-standard HTTP methods to:
1. Bypass security controls or Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) that specifically filter certain methods
2. Exploit HTTP request smuggling vulnerabilities in reverse proxies
3. Perform CSRF attacks by disguising requests as GET requests
4. Trigger unintended application logic if code contains conditional method handling
5. Evade logging and monitoring systems that only track specific HTTP methods

In the context of the get_favorite_restaurants endpoint which handles sensitive user data, allowing DELETE or PUT methods could potentially trigger data modification if combined with other vulnerabilities like IDOR (which is already documented for this endpoint).
references:
CWE-405: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames (related to method handling)
OWASP: HTTP Method Violation
RFC 7231: HTTP/1.1 Semantics and Content (Section 4.3: Request Methods)
